# CORE-TGT-01

**Is every catalogued artefact the design uses at target or in flight, never retired, and does each one still at baseline have a decision naming what it moves to?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [Core architecture lens](core.md) 0.6.0 |
| Area | TGT: Target state |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A tool, by its rule |
| Reads | `elements`, `decisions.departure`, `triage.target_state` |

## Why it matters

A design that builds on what the target state retires spends money moving away from where the organisation has decided to go.

## Rule

Take each building block's target-state position as the responsible architect attested it, from the triage record's target_state, or from the catalogue's lifecycle_state where an architect maintains it. Neither the author nor an assessor infers a position. No element is at retired. Every element at baseline, retiring, contained or not-target is named in the affects of a decision with departure set; a not-target element brings in technology the target does not plan for, and a contained one is extended to a use the target does not plan for, so its departure says why it cannot wait for a target alternative. Where a position carries a permitted_use, an element used beyond it is a departure too, and a reviewer judges the use against the limit. An element with no attested position leaves this criterion not-assessed for that element, and the missing attestation becomes a condition.
